title: ToolStarted
description: A tool invocation began. Emitted for **every** tool, including the ones no human was asked about — the audit trail is anchored on the same hook, for exactly that reason (ADR-011).

toolUseId.description: The engine's id for this invocation. It is what ties started, progress and completed together.

kind.description: The canonical kind of the tool, decided by the adapter of the engine: `file.read`, `file.edit`, `file.write`, `file.delete`, `file.move`, `search`, `shell`, `shell.output`, `web.fetch`, `web.search`, `mcp`, `agent`, `question`, `plan`, `tasks`, `other`. **Open**: a kind the client does not know is drawn as the generic line, never an error (ADR-025).

label.description: The label of the row, built by the backend.

subject.description: What the call is about, normalised.

changes.description: The files the call changes — what turns on the diff. Empty for a kind that changes no file.

origin.description: The engine and its own name for the tool — opaque.

rawInput.description: The exact input the tool was called with, **opaque**: shown whole as the exact input and exported, and no client reads a field of it (plan 28, D-04). Everything a client draws comes from `label`, `subject` and `changes`.

interaction.description: On a `question` or a `plan`: what it asks, normalised by the adapter — the same the `permission.requested` of the call carries, so the history draws it without the raw input (plan 28, B-21). Absent on every other kind.

title.description: A short human label for the invocation, already derived by the backend: the description the model gave the call, when it is non-blank text. Absent otherwise, and the client shows the `label` alone.

parentToolUseId.description: Set when this comes from a subagent: the `toolUseId` of the `agent` call that opened it. Absent on the main conversation.

at.description: When the entry was written, ISO 8601 — on the events of the history only, from the transcript's own `timestamp`. It marks the **end** of what the entry holds, never its start: a duration read from two of them is an upper bound. Absent live, where the frame's `ts` is the clock, and on an entry the store recorded no time for.
